messages:
ryan (Sales): Heads up — big finance prospect sent a security questionnaire and wants a security review call this week. They care about RBAC, audit logging, and BYOK/KMS. Can someone take point?

alice (SecEng): I can do the questionnaire. Do we have a current RBAC matrix and an example audit log schema ready?

ben (SRE): We have a draft RBAC matrix in the eng docs but it's out-of-date for Dedicated customers. Quick note: Dedicated supports role scoping per-tenant already, but we'll need to confirm admin/engineer/read-only labels.

ryan (Sales): Customer specifically asked for separation of duties and proof that support engineering cannot access customer keys.

diana (Product): For separation of duties, we should highlight Dedicated + Private modes + KMS integration. We need a short blurb about how key access is restricted and logged.

alice (SecEng): Draft blurb: "Customer keys (BYOK) are never exported from customer KMS. Redwood stores only key references; cryptographic ops happen in HSM-backed processes and access is logged. Support engineers require an approved access request and approval workflow; ephemeral access is timeboxed and fully audited." Thoughts?

ben (SRE): +1. Add the specific audit fields they asked for. Example audit entry we can share: 
```
{ "timestamp": "2024-06-01T14:12:03Z", "actor": "service-account:redwood-kms-connector", "action": "Encrypt", "resource": "customer/keys/123", "request_id": "req-abc123", "result": "Success", "ip": "10.0.0.5" }
```

alice (SecEng): Good. Also include retention policy: audit logs retained 1 year by default for Hosted, configurable for Dedicated/Private, and can be forwarded to customer SIEM via syslog or S3 export.

maria (GTM): The customer also wants SOC2 cert and pen test reports. Do we have the latest artifacts to attach?

diana (Product): I have the SOC2 cover letter and the redacted pen test summary. I'll attach the links to the questionnaire. <https://drive.company/reports/soc2-2024>

ryan (Sales): Nice. They also want to know our vuln triage timeline and SLA for critical findings.

alice (SecEng): Triage process: initial ack within 2 hours for critical, 24h for high. Emergency incident response team engaged for critical. Mean time to mitigation depends on the vuln class; we commit to mitigations or compensating controls within 72 hours for critical customer-impacting issues unless mitigation requires patch from third parties.

ben (SRE): Add that we have automated CVE monitoring, weekly dependency scans, and an internal Kanban for remediation.

ryan (Sales): Great. Can we set a security review call Thurs at 2pm PT? Customer asked for a short demo of audit logs + KMS flow.

alice (SecEng): I'm available. ben?

ben (SRE): Can do. I'll prepare a short walkthrough and a small demo script showing an Encrypt request flow and the resulting audit entry.

alice (SecEng): I'll fill out the questionnaire answers for RBAC, audit logging, incident response, and attach the SOC2/pen test links. I'll also include the KMS integration diagram.

maria (GTM): I'll join the call to handle contract/security questions and to reassure them on SLAs.

sec-bot: Reminder — attachable artifacts checklist: SOC2, pen-test summary, RBAC matrix, audit-schema, KMS-integration-diagram, incident-contact-list.

ryan (Sales): Perfect. Assigning action items: alice — questionnaire + attachments; ben — demo and RBAC confirmation; diana — attach artifacts; maria — join call; me — schedule meeting and send customer invite.

alice (SecEng): Will do. I'll post the filled questionnaire link here once complete. :thumbsup:

ben (SRE): Demo script TODO: 1) show encrypt call 2) show log line 3) show access request workflow. Planning to use staging Dedicated env.

ryan (Sales): Thanks team — I'll create the calendar invite for Thu 2024-06-06 14:00 PT and include the questionnaire PDF.

alice (SecEng): One more thing — customer asked if we support KMS rotation and whether re-encryption is required. Short answer: rotation supported via key aliasing; re-encryption not required for data encrypted with envelope keys because we encrypt data keys with the master key which is rotated. I'll add a short appendix.

ryan (Sales): Awesome. Close the loop here when the questionnaire link is posted.

alice (SecEng): Link posted: <https://docs.company/qna/enterprise-finance-0614> - contains answers + audit examples + attachments.

ryan (Sales): Received. I'll confirm the call with the customer. :rocket:
